title: Your Child's Little Heart Knows Allah Through Love
summary:
You gaze into your child's bright eyes as they point to a colorful butterfly fluttering in the garden, or marvel at the golden sunrise. You wonder how you can plant deep faith in Allah in their little heart, a faith that begins with love and hope, balancing love and reverence without alienating fear, and becomes their support throughout life. At this age, children's minds open to big questions of existence, and they begin to form their first perceptions of the world and who runs it. These simple daily moments are your golden opportunity to introduce Allah to your child as the most beloved and generous One they will ever know.

The sound innate disposition (fitrah) inclines towards belief in the Creator, and our role as parents is to nourish this disposition with love and beauty. Instead of starting with threats and warnings, we begin by introducing Allah through His magnificent signs in the universe: Who created this beautiful flower? Who made the bird sing? Who sent down the rain to water the earth? All these questions lead the child, by their innate disposition, to the answer: "Allah." Most importantly, we instill in their heart that Allah is "The First," before Whom there was nothing, and He is the Creator of everything, and that He, glory be to Him, is Generous and Merciful and loves us. Always remember that a child opens their heart to love before anything else, and this is part of the Prophet's ﷺ general methodology in calling to Allah and teaching, and it is even more fitting with children, for the Prophet ﷺ said: «Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not repel people» (Sahih al-Bukhari 69).

So, make every new discovery an opportunity to connect your child with their loving Creator. Do not hesitate to answer their curious questions with an open heart, even if they seem difficult. Be calm and confident, and remember that your goal is to build a bridge of love between your child and their Lord, a bridge that extends through the grandeur of His creation and the beauty of His mercy. In this way, you help your child grow up upon firm faith, by Allah's will, filled with tranquility and gratitude, enabling them to see the traces of Allah's mercy in every detail of their life, knowing Him as a merciful Lord and a supporting Guardian, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿ٱللَّهُ وَلِيُّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 257] (interpretation of the meaning: "Allah is the ally of those who believe").
try_this: Tonight: Before bed, talk with your child about the most beautiful thing they saw today (a flower, a cloud, a toy), and ask them: "Who created all this beauty?" Then say with them: "Allahu Akbar, how magnificent is Allah!" and hug them tenderly.
reflection_prompts: How can I answer my child's question "Who created Allah?" in a simple and reassuring way without making them feel their question is wrong?
What daily moments can I utilize to introduce my child to Allah through the beauty of His creation and His mercy?
parent_script: «Look, my dear, who created this beautiful flower to make us happy? It is Allah, He loves us very much.»
